ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two parallel transmission lines. The current at the left end of the upper line is labeled I1, and the current at the right end is labeled I3; the current at the left end of the lower line is labeled I2, and the current at the right end is labeled I4. Among the candidate positions, Q is located toward the left of the upper line, S is located toward the right of the upper line, and R is located toward the left of the lower line. The phasor diagram below draws V1, V2, I1, I2, I3, and I4 under the same reference: I2 is roughly leftward, I4 is roughly down-right, and the two are approximately opposite; I1 points to the right and has a relatively large magnitude, I3 points up-right and has a relatively small magnitude, and the two are not approximately 180° apart. Reasoning: For a healthy line, the currents at the two ends should mainly appear as through current, and under the same reference the current phasors at the two ends are approximately 180° opposite. Therefore, I2 and I4 being approximately opposite indicates that the lower line is the healthy path. I1 and I3 of the upper line do not cancel each other, indicating that the fault is on this upper line circuit. Comparing the fault current feed-in amounts further, the upper-line current I1 at the left end is clearly greater than the upper-line current I3 at the right end, which is equivalent to the impedance seen from the left end to the fault point being smaller, so the fault is closer to the left end. The marked position toward the left of the upper line is Q.

raw_record.question_text: A sustained three-phase fault occurs in the power system shown in the image. The current and voltage phasors during the fault (on a common reference), after the natural transients have died down, are also shown. Where is the fault located?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: two parallel lines, upper-line end currents I1 and I3, lower-line end currents I2 and I4, with voltage phasors V1 and V2 shown on the same reference. Then compare the current phasors by line. Since I2 and I4 are almost 180 degrees apart, treat the lower line as the healthy through path. Since I1 and I3 are not cancelling, identify the upper line as the faulted line. Finally use the relative feed: the left-end upper-line current I1 is larger than the right-end current I3, equivalently the left-side apparent impedance to the fault is smaller, so the upper-line fault is nearer the left end. The labeled upper-line near-left location is Q.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses current continuity/current-differential behavior of the two parallel lines first, then a simple relative-distance inference. This route mainly relies on comparing end-current phasors on each line, not on forming detailed apparent impedances.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the one-line diagram as two parallel transmission lines between left and right sources, with measured currents I1 and I3 entering the upper line from the left and right ends, and I2 and I4 entering the lower line from the left and right ends. Read the phasor plot: I2 and I4 are nearly opposite, while I1 and I3 are not opposite and both point generally toward the fault-feeding direction; I1 is larger than I3. The possible fault labels include Q on the upper line near the left side and other labels on/near the other line or side.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text facts that the fault is a sustained three-phase fault, that transients have died out, and that all current and voltage phasors are drawn on a common reference, allowing direct steady-state phasor comparison.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a sustained balanced three-phase fault after transients, use steady-state phasors. On an unfaulted line section with negligible shunt current, the currents entering from the two ends should be equal and opposite. On the faulted line, currents from both ends feed the fault, so their phasor sum is nonzero. If the same type of source and line impedances are assumed, the larger feeding current/apparent smaller impedance side indicates the fault is closer to that terminal.

method.method_draft: First describe the image and assign each current to its line and terminal. For each candidate line, form the apparent impedance from each terminal voltage and the current entering that line: upper line uses V1/I1 and V2/I3; lower line uses V1/I2 and V2/I4, with the given current reference directions. The upper-line pairs have voltage-current angular separations consistent with positive inductive line drops from each source to a fault, while the lower-line pairs would imply an inconsistent/reverse apparent impedance for at least one end. Thus the fault is on the upper line. Then compare the apparent impedance magnitudes visually: |V1|/|I1| is smaller than |V2|/|I3| because I1 is large relative to V1 and I3 is smaller relative to V2. Hence the fault is closer to the left terminal on the upper line, which is labeled Q.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是左右两个电源通过两条并联 transmission line 相连。左侧端母线标有 P，并给出左端电压相量 V1；右侧端给出右端电压相量 V2。上方线路上标有候选位置 Q（靠左）和 S（靠右），下方线路上标有候选位置 R（靠左）。电流分配为：I1 在上线路左端，参考方向从左端进入上线路；I3 在上线路右端，参考方向从右端进入上线路；I2 在下线路左端，参考方向对应下线路左端电流；I4 在下线路右端，参考方向从右端进入下线路。下方相量图中，V1 和 V2 都大致向上，I1 向右且幅值较大，I3 向右上且幅值较小于 I1，I2 大致向左，I4 向右下。
推理：按给定方法，对每条候选线路用端电压除以进入该线路的端电流来判断 apparent impedance。若故障在某条实际线路上，则从两端看向故障点的 apparent impedance 应表现为正的感性线路阻抗。上线路的两端组合是 V1/I1 和 V2/I3：从相量图看，V1 相对 I1 超前形成正感性角度，V2 相对 I3 也形成正感性角度，因此上线路两端判断一致。下线路的两端组合是 V1/I2 和 V2/I4：其中至少 V1/I2 会给出与正常正感性线路压降不一致的反向/负角度 apparent impedance，因此下线路不符合。故障应在上线路。接着比较上线路两端到故障点的阻抗距离：|V1|/|I1| 视觉上小于 |V2|/|I3|，因为 I1 相对于 V1 较大，而 I3 相对于 V2 较小。因此从左端到故障点的 apparent impedance 较小，故障更靠近上线路左端。上线路靠左的标注位置是 Q。
最终答案：Location Q

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses an impedance-to-fault test from each terminal: check which current-voltage pair gives physically plausible positive line impedances and then compare their magnitudes for distance. It does not primarily identify the healthy line by current cancellation, although that can be a consistency check.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the image the terminal voltage phasors V1 and V2, both roughly upward, and the four current phasors: I1 to the right/slightly down, I3 to the right/up, I2 to the left, and I4 to the right/down. Also read the topology and labels: I1/I3 belong to the upper transmission line, I2/I4 to the lower line, and Q is on the upper line closer to the left terminal than the right terminal.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that the phasors are during the sustained fault after natural transients have died down; this justifies treating V/I ratios as steady-state apparent impedances rather than transient quantities.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a solid or low-impedance balanced three-phase fault on a line, the terminal voltage to the fault is approximately the series positive-sequence line impedance times the current feeding the fault from that terminal: Z_app = V/I. A valid faulted-line current should give an apparent impedance with the inductive line-impedance angle and a positive distance. The smaller magnitude of Z_app corresponds to the closer terminal.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two parallel transmission lines. The current at the left end of the upper line is labeled I1, and the current at the right end is labeled I3; the current at the left end of the lower line is labeled I2, and the current at the right end is labeled I4. Among the candidate positions, Q is located toward the left of the upper line, S is located toward the right of the upper line, and R is located toward the left of the lower line. The phasor diagram below draws V1, V2, I1, I2, I3, and I4 under the same reference: I2 is roughly leftward, I4 is roughly down-right, and the two are approximately opposite; I1 points to the right and has a relatively large magnitude, I3 points up-right and has a relatively small magnitude, and the two are not approximately 180° apart. Reasoning: For a healthy line, the currents at the two ends should mainly appear as through current, and under the same reference the current phasors at the two ends are approximately 180° opposite. Therefore, I2 and I4 being approximately opposite indicates that the lower line is the healthy path. I1 and I3 of the upper line do not cancel each other, indicating that the fault is on this upper line circuit. Comparing the fault current feed-in amounts further, the upper-line current I1 at the left end is clearly greater than the upper-line current I3 at the right end, which is equivalent to the impedance seen from the left end to the fault point being smaller, so the fault is closer to the left end. The marked position toward the left of the upper line is Q.
